highlights: 8 Weeks of comprehensive 3D motion graphics and product animation training (64 guided learning hours)
Master Cinema 4D interface, parametric modeling, splines, deformers, and hierarchy management
Professional keyframe animation: timing, spacing, anticipation, follow-through, and F-curve easing
MoGraph procedural systems: Cloner distributions, Effectors (Plain, Random, Step, Delay), and Fields
Introductory dynamics: rigid-body collisions, gravity, bounce, simple cloth, and simulation caching
Redshift look development: OpenPBR materials, studio product lighting (3-point & HDRI), and render passes
Commercial product animation: packaging reveals, camera choreography, and branded 3D typography
Coordinated 3-part commercial portfolio: procedural motion loop, 15–20s product animation, and 3D title sequence with editable .c4d source files

hands_on_tech.primary_tool: Maxon Cinema 4D (MoGraph, Cloner, Effectors, Fields, Timeline, F-Curves, Dynamics)
hands_on_tech.renderer: Redshift (OpenPBR Shaders, Redshift Live, Area Lights, Dome HDRI, AOVs)
supporting_tools: Adobe Illustrator (Vector logos, packaging artwork, and spline paths)
Adobe After Effects (Optional finishing, color refinement, and sequence compilation)

learning_outcomes: Navigate Cinema 4D viewports, docks, and managers with speed and confidence.
Work effectively with 3D coordinate systems, object axes, and parent-child scene hierarchies.
Create foundational 3D models using parametric primitives, splines, and generators.
Apply non-destructive deformers (Bend, Twist, Taper, Spline Wrap) to shape geometry.
Set and edit transformation keyframes (position, rotation, scale) on the animation timeline.
Apply core animation principles: timing, spacing, anticipation, and follow-through.
Refine motion easing and speed transitions using the Timeline F-Curve editor.
Construct procedural clone arrays using the MoGraph Cloner (Linear, Radial, Grid, Object).
Apply MoGraph Effectors (Plain, Random, Step, Delay) to control transform properties.
Use Fields (Linear, Spherical, Box, Falloffs) and field layers to drive procedural animations.
Build reusable procedural motion setups with exposed parametric controls.
Understand basic node-based procedural concepts in Nodes Fields and Effectors.
Set up introductory rigid-body dynamics with active and passive collision tags.
Configure mass, friction, bounce, and gravity for stable physical simulations.
Experiment with simple soft-body deformation and basic cloth draping behaviors.
Cache dynamics and MoGraph simulations for reproducible, glitch-free playback and rendering.
Model and assemble commercial product models, bottles, containers, and packaging.
Build physically plausible shaders using modern Redshift OpenPBR materials.
Create studio lighting setups (key, fill, rim, and HDRI dome) for commercial products.
Compose product cameras with appropriate focal lengths, depth of field, and motion blur.
Configure Redshift render settings, adaptive sampling, and noise thresholds for animation.
Utilize Redshift render passes (AOVs) for multipass compositing and color management.
Create animated 3D typography and brand titles using MoText and spline extrusions.
Package complete, portable Cinema 4D project archives using Save Project with Assets.
Analyze commercial creative briefs, develop storyboards, and execute client revisions.
Present 3D motion-design decisions, F-curve curves, and procedural logic professionally.
Deliver client-ready animation renders formatted for broadcast, web, and social advertising.

faq.question: Is this Cinema 4D course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: The course starts with Cinema 4D fundamentals and progresses into modeling, animation, MoGraph, and Redshift rendering. Basic design, composition, or animation knowledge is recommended.

faq.question: What will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn Cinema 4D modeling, keyframes, F-curves, MoGraph Cloners, Effectors, Fields, introductory dynamics, Redshift lighting, and commercial product animation.

faq.question: What is MoGraph?
faq.answer: MoGraph is Cinema 4D's procedural motion graphics system. It allows artists to create and control complex arrays of animated objects through Cloners, Effectors, Fields, and related procedural tools.

faq.question: Will I learn procedural animation?
faq.answer: Yes. Procedural MoGraph is a core pillar of the course. Students create original, reusable procedural animation systems rather than relying on premade templates.

faq.question: Will I learn 3D product animation?
faq.answer: Yes. You will model, shade, light, and animate an approximately 15–20-second commercial product or packaging animation based on an industry-style brief.

faq.question: What portfolio projects will I create?
faq.answer: You will complete an original procedural motion loop, a premium product animation, and a short 3D title or brand-motion sequence, supported by editable files and rendering breakdowns.

faq.question: Will I learn Redshift?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces Redshift OpenPBR materials, studio lighting, cameras, render optimization, AOVs, and professional output workflows.

faq.question: Is Redshift included with Cinema 4D?
faq.answer: Maxon's current Cinema 4D subscription offering includes Redshift. Exact feature access and hardware compatibility depend on the applicable subscription, installation, and workstation GPU.

faq.question: Will I learn dynamics and simulations?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers introductory rigid-body dynamics, collisions, simple soft-body/cloth awareness, and simulation caching. Advanced fluid or destruction simulations are excluded.

faq.question: Does the course include Cinema 4D 2027 features?
faq.answer: The course introduces applicable procedural Scatter, Nodes Fields/Effectors, and Redshift improvements where supported. Fundamental MoGraph and keyframing skills remain the core learning requirement.

faq.question: Do I need After Effects knowledge?
faq.answer: No. After Effects may be used for limited sequence finishing where available, but it is not a mandatory advanced prerequisite.

faq.question: Is this course part of 3D Academy or Video & Motion Academy?
faq.answer: The course belongs to Nova Skills' 3D Academy. It also complements relevant Motion Graphics courses in Video & Motion Academy (Course 69 and Course 72).

faq.question: Will I learn character animation?
faq.answer: This certification focuses on 3D motion graphics and commercial product animation. Complex character rigging and character animation pipelines are outside its scope.

faq.question: Do students create original animations?
faq.answer: Yes. Assessed work must demonstrate original modeling, keyframes, and meaningful procedural animation systems rather than downloaded-template replacement alone.

faq.question: Are Cinema 4D and supporting software licenses included?
faq.answer: Software access depends on Nova Skills' verified training arrangements. Students receive guidance on accessing Maxon educational or trial licensing where eligible.

faq.question: What is the course duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course lasts eight weeks, includes 64 guided learning hours, and has a listed fee of ₹11,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
